Obscurity

/uhb-SKYOOR-ih-tee/ - the stress falls on SKYOOR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Obscurity means the state of being unknown, hidden, or forgotten.

The chess variant spent decades in obscurity before a streaming series made it a lunchtime craze.

Worked Example

Most words live and die in obscurity. 'Snollygoster' had its brief career in 1890s newsprint, then sank: no textbook carried it, no speech revived it, and only dictionary editors, turning the yellowed pages, ever met it again.

Obscurity is exact for that sunk-from-view state: the word still exists - a determined reader can find it - but nobody knows it, uses it, or misses it. Not anonymity (a name kept off known work) and not yet oblivion (erased even from the dictionary): obscurity is the wide, quiet shelf between.

How Obscurity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

anonymity

anonymity: the name is unknown; the work might be famous

namelessness

namelessness: the plain word for having no name attached

Antonyms

fame

fame: widely known and talked about

limelight

limelight: the bright center of public attention

How Strong Is It? — anonymity → obscurity → oblivion

anonymity vs. obscurity

anonymity vs. obscurity: Anonymity hides only the name - a donor can stay unnamed while the gift makes headlines; obscurity goes further, leaving the person and the work unknown alike.

oblivion vs. obscurity

oblivion vs. obscurity: Oblivion outdoes obscurity: an obscure poet still sits findable on a library shelf, while a poet in oblivion has vanished from every shelf and every memory.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ob-

Prefix — ob-: over, against

Root — scur

Root — scur: covered, dark

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state of

Put it together

Put it together: Ob- (over) + scur (covered, dark) + -ity (state of) = the state of being covered over. Latin obscurus described what shadow had covered; obscurity is that shadow settled on a person, a word, or a hot spring no guidebook has found.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Obscurity is built on Latin obscurus, 'covered over, darkened.' The old covering-root behind -scur- made no other common English word: its only living relatives are obscure and obscurity themselves, so this family tree stops after one branch.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Obscurity names the state of being unknown or forgotten - careers begin in it and often end in it. Anonymity hides only the name; a person in obscurity is unknown, work and all. And keep the mirror straight: obscurity means the world overlooks you; oblivious (this unit) means you overlook the world.
